question.value: What do deep JWST/NIRCam images of SN 1987A reveal about its ejecta, equatorial ring and exterior emission, and what are the sources (dust, synchrotron, lines) of the NIR emission?

evidence.quote: In the NIRCam images, we identify: 1) faint H$_2$ crescents, which are emissions located between the ejecta and the equatorial ring, 2) a bar, which is a substructure of the ejecta
on 2021 November 2nd as part of the Project 2021.1.00707.S

The synthesized beam was 0.081"$\times$0.061" with a position angle of 33.7$^{\circ}$ for the major axis.
The shortest baselines allowed for a maximum recoverable scale of 0.993".
The total integration time was 10,813 sec.

analysis_steps.goal: Measure NIR SEDs and power-law indices in apertures

method.value: Extract fluxes in several apertures after subtracting a blank-sky background, fit F_nu ∝ nu^-alpha to F323N, F356W, F444W

evidence.loc: 3.3 Power-law spectra at 3–4 μm in the equatorial ring and its exterior
evidence.quote: The fluxes at F323N, F356W and F444W follow a power-law continuum across SN 1987A (black lines in Fig [11](#fig:SED)).

validation.value: compared with radio-to-ALMA SED power law alpha=0.70

evidence.quote: the grey line shows the power-law of $\alpha=0.70$ crossing the 8.7 GHz flux at day=10,942
The calibration software version number was 1.8.5 with CRDS version 11.16.16
Simulated PSFs were calculated using WebbPSF (cite: Perrin2014).
The convolution was processed, using the python code PSF Matching (cite: Gordon2008; Aniano2011).

results_numeric.quantity: Power-law index of ejecta at 3–4 micron

evidence.quote: The ejecta have the steepest power-law index $\alpha$ at a value of 3.1

results_numeric.quantity: Power-law index at hot spots / diffuse emission

evidence.quote: The power-law indices are as small as $\alpha=1.6$ at the hot spots on the ring and $\alpha=1.5$ within the diffuse emission.

results_numeric.quantity: Power-law index at western / eastern outer spots

evidence.quote: The power-law indices are $\alpha=2.9$ and 1.9 at the western and eastern outer spots, respectively.

results_numeric.quantity: Minimum magnetic field for synchrotron break at 3 micron

evidence.quote: Having the break wavelength/frequency to be at 3 $\mu$m  requires the magnetic field of $B\ge2.1$ mG.

findings_qualitative.value: 3–5 micron continuum in ring and exterior has substantial synchrotron contribution; dust emission is confined to outer spots and diffuse emission

evidence.quote: In the ring and exterior to the ring, synchrotron emission contributes a substantial fraction to the continuum.

claims.hypothesis: Is the 3–5 micron emission in the ring and exterior synchrotron?
claims.experiment: Compared NIRCam SEDs with the radio/ALMA power law and MIRI dust images
claims.result: Radio power law with alpha=0.70 matches the F323N and F356W fluxes; hot spots have little 7 micron dust
claims.finding: Synchrotron contributes substantially to the NIR continuum

evidence.quote: the grey line can explain the F323N and F356W fluxes very well, showing that a substantial fraction of the NIR fluxes is synchrotron emission.

limitations_admitted.value: ALMA 315 GHz flux likely underestimated because of the small maximum recoverable scale

evidence.quote: The ALMA flux at 315 GHz is probably underestimated, because the interferometry had a fully recoverable size of only $0.99''$

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA used only qualitatively and for one flux point; calibration unstated
Synchrotron versus dust attribution relies on a power-law comparison with no formal fit

data_public_as_stated.value: JWST pipeline-reduced data on MAST; ALMA data availability not stated

evidence.quote: The pipeline reduced data are available at MIKULSKI archive (<http://dx.doi.org/10.17909/dzkq-7c90>).
